key_insight: Hodge–de Rham PINNs augment neural PDE solvers with differential-form structure to represent topology-induced behavior that conventional potential-based PINNs can miss.
engineering_relevance: This approach could improve physics-informed modeling on domains with holes, punctures, or voids where nonzero circulation and path dependence matter.
method: Parameterize a 1-form using the Hodge–Morrey–Friedrichs decomposition for manifolds with boundary.
Train with an associated PDE loss and connect the learned form to scalar solutions through integral operators.
Use exhaustion functions when the loss integrability condition is not met.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees and experiments on topologically adverse problems, including the Aharonov–Bohm effect, inexact forms, and nontrivial harmonic and coexact components, but gives no quantitative results.
watch_item: The operator connecting form-based and potential-based problems may require nontrivial integration or case-specific analysis, complicating implementation.
paper_title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
